mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (>4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with disinflation, which increases risk aversion and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals a shift from spending to saving and a housing market pullback, reducing near-term consumption and investment, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises >10% and HOUST falls >10% over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a credit crunch.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid wage inflation (>5% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a synchronized economic expansion.
